sentences.zh: 王艮，字敬止，吉水人。

translations.literal: Wang Gen, styled Jingzhi, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gen, whose style was Jingzhi, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 建文二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jianwen reign he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the second year of the Jianwen reign.

sentences.zh: 對策第一。

translations.literal: In the policy essay he ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: His answers in the palace examination placed him first.

sentences.zh: 貌寢，易以胡靖，即胡廣也。

translations.literal: His appearance was unprepossessing, so he was replaced by Hu Jing, who was Hu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Because his looks were plain, the top place was given to Hu Jing—better known as Hu Guang.

sentences.zh: 艮次之，又次李貫。

translations.literal: Gen came next, and after him Li Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Gen ranked second, with Li Guan third.

sentences.zh: 三人皆同里，並授修撰，如洪武中故事，設文史館居之。

translations.literal: All three were from the same district; they were jointly appointed compilers, and following the precedent of the Hongwu era a Literary and Historical Office was established for them to reside in.
translations.idiomatic: All three were fellow townsmen and were appointed compilers together; following Hongwu precedent, a Literary and Historical Office was set up for them to live in.

sentences.zh: 預修《太祖實錄》及《類要》、《時政記》諸書。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor, the Classified Essentials, the Record of Current Affairs, and other works.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of Taizu, the Classified Essentials, the Record of Current Affairs, and other state books.

sentences.zh: 一時大著作皆綜理之。

translations.literal: For a time all major literary projects were coordinated under him.
translations.idiomatic: For a time he oversaw every major literary project at court.

sentences.zh: 數上書言時務。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of the day.
translations.idiomatic: He sent up many memorials on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 燕兵薄京城，艮與妻子訣曰：「食人之祿者，死人之事。

translations.literal: When the Yan army pressed close to the capital, Gen took leave of his wife and children, saying: "One who eats another's stipend must die for that person's cause.
translations.idiomatic: As the Yan forces neared the capital, Gen bade farewell to his wife and children, saying, "Whoever lives on another man's pay must die for his lord's sake.

sentences.zh: 吾不可復生矣。」

translations.literal: I can no longer go on living.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot go on living.

sentences.zh: 解縉、吳溥與艮、靖比舍居。

translations.literal: Xie Jin, Wu Pu, Gen, and Jing lived in neighboring houses.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jin and Wu Pu lived next door to Gen and Jing.

sentences.zh: 城陷前一夕，皆集溥舍。

translations.literal: On the eve before the city fell, they all gathered at Pu's house.
translations.idiomatic: On the night before the city fell, they all met at Pu's home.

sentences.zh: 縉陳說大義，靖亦奮激慷慨，艮獨流涕不言。

translations.literal: Jin expounded the great principle; Jing too was stirred and impassioned, while Gen alone wept in silence and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin spoke fervently of duty; Jing too grew heated and bold, while Gen only wept and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 三人去，溥子與弼尚幼，嘆曰：「胡叔能死，是大佳事。」

translations.literal: When the three had gone, Pu's sons You and Bi were still young; he sighed and said: "If Uncle Hu can die, that would be a fine thing indeed."
translations.idiomatic: After they left, Pu's young sons You and Bi sighed and said, "If Uncle Hu can die for the cause, that would be splendid."

sentences.zh: 溥曰：「不然，獨王叔死耳。」

translations.literal: Pu said: "Not so—only Uncle Wang will die."
translations.idiomatic: Pu replied, "No—only Uncle Wang will die."

sentences.zh: 語未畢，隔墻聞靖呼：「外喧甚，謹視豚。」

translations.literal: Before he had finished speaking, from beyond the wall they heard Jing call out: "There is a great uproar outside—mind the pig carefully."
translations.idiomatic: He had barely finished when they heard Jing shout through the wall, "It's very noisy outside—watch the pig closely."

sentences.zh: 溥顧與弼曰：「一豚尚不能舍，肯舍生乎？」

translations.literal: Pu turned to Bi and said: "If he cannot give up a single pig, will he give up his life?"
translations.idiomatic: Pu turned to Bi and said, "A man who cannot part with one pig—will he part with his life?"

sentences.zh: 須臾艮舍哭，飲鴆死矣。

translations.literal: Before long came weeping from Gen's house; he had drunk poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward wailing rose from Gen's house—he had taken poison and died.

sentences.zh: 縉馳謁，成祖甚喜。

translations.literal: Jin hurried to pay his respects; Chengzu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jin rushed to present himself, and Chengzu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 明日薦靖，召至，叩頭謝。

translations.literal: The next day he recommended Jing; Jing was summoned, came forward, and kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jin recommended Jing, who was summoned, came forward, and kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 貫亦迎附。

translations.literal: Guan too came forward to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Guan also came over to the new regime.

sentences.zh: 後成祖出建文時群臣封事千余通，令縉等編閱。

translations.literal: Later Chengzu produced more than a thousand sealed memorials from Jianwen's ministers and ordered Jin and the others to sort through them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chengzu brought out more than a thousand sealed memorials from Jianwen's ministers and had Jin and others review them.

sentences.zh: 事涉兵農、錢谷者留之，諸言語幹犯及他，一切皆焚毀。

translations.literal: Those touching on military affairs, agriculture, and revenue were kept; all that were verbally offensive or otherwise were burned.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials on war, farming, and finance were kept; anything insulting or otherwise objectionable was burned.

sentences.zh: 因從容問貫、縉等曰：「爾等宜皆有之。」

translations.literal: Then, speaking at ease, he asked Guan, Jin, and the rest: "You surely all had such memorials among you."
translations.idiomatic: Then he asked Guan, Jin, and the others casually, "You must all have had such papers yourselves."

sentences.zh: 眾未對，貫獨頓首曰：「臣實未嘗有也。」

translations.literal: No one answered; Guan alone kowtowed and said: "Your subject truly never had any."
translations.idiomatic: No one answered until Guan alone kowtowed and said, "I truly never had any."

sentences.zh: 成祖曰：「爾以無為美耶？

translations.literal: Chengzu said: "Do you take having none as something fine?
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu said, "You think having none is admirable?

sentences.zh: 食其祿，任其事，當國家危急，官近侍獨無一言可乎？

translations.literal: You eat the stipend and bear the office—when the state was in peril, could a close attendant truly have had not a single word to say?
translations.idiomatic: You took the pay and held the post—when the realm was in crisis, could a close attendant really have had nothing to say?

sentences.zh: 朕特惡夫誘建文壞祖法亂政者耳。」

translations.literal: I particularly hate only those who led Jianwen to ruin ancestral institutions and throw government into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: I only hate those who led Jianwen to overturn ancestral law and throw the government into chaos.

sentences.zh: 後貫遷中允，坐累，死獄中。

translations.literal: Later Guan was promoted to Right Assistant Censor, but through implication in a case he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guan was made Right Assistant Censor, but through implication in a case he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 臨卒嘆曰：「吾愧王敬止矣。」

translations.literal: On the verge of death he sighed: "I am ashamed before Wang Jingzhi."
translations.idiomatic: As he lay dying he sighed, "I am ashamed before Wang Jingzhi."

sentences.zh: 有高遜誌者，艮座主也，蕭縣人，寓嘉興。

translations.literal: There was Gao Xunzhi, Gen's chief examiner, a native of Xiaoxian who had settled in Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: There was Gao Xunzhi, Gen's chief examiner, from Xiaoxian, who lived in Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 幼嗜學，師貢師泰、周伯琦等。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and studied under Gong Shitai, Zhou Boqi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he loved study and took Gong Shitai, Zhou Boqi, and others as his teachers.

sentences.zh: 文章典雅，成一家言。

translations.literal: His writing was refined and elegant, forming a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was refined and distinctive, forming a school of his own.

sentences.zh: 征修《元史》，入翰林，累遷試吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Summoned to help compile the History of Yuan, he entered the Hanlin Academy and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Called to help compile the History of Yuan, he entered the Hanlin and rose to Acting Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以事謫朐山。

translations.literal: Because of an affair he was banished to Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a case he was banished to Qushan.

sentences.zh: 建文初，召為太常少卿，與董倫同主會試。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites and, together with Dong Lun, presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwen he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites and, with Dong Lun, ran the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 得士自艮外，胡靖、吳溥、楊榮、金幼孜、楊溥、胡濙、顧佐等皆為名臣。

translations.literal: Among those who passed, apart from Gen, Hu Jing, Wu Pu, Yang Rong, Jin Youzi, Yang Pu, Hu Ying, Gu Zuo, and others all became famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Besides Gen, those chosen included Hu Jing, Wu Pu, Yang Rong, Jin Youzi, Yang Pu, Hu Ying, and Gu Zuo—all later famous ministers.

sentences.zh: 燕師入，存歿無可考。

translations.literal: When the Yan army entered the capital, whether he lived or died cannot be ascertained.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces entered the capital, whether he lived or died cannot be determined.

sentences.zh: 廖升，襄陽人。

translations.literal: Liao Sheng was a native of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Sheng came from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 不知其所以進，學行最知名，與方孝孺、王紳相友善。

translations.literal: How he advanced is unknown; in learning and conduct he was the most renowned, and he was on friendly terms with Fang Xiaoru and Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: How he rose is unknown, but in learning and conduct he was the most celebrated, and he was close to Fang Xiaoru and Wang Shen.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，由左府斷事擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the end of the Hongwu reign, from an adjudicator in the Left Secretariat he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Hongwu he was promoted from an adjudicator in the Left Secretariat to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 建文初，修《太祖實錄》，董倫、王景為總裁官；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen, in compiling the Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor, Dong Lun and Wang Jing served as chief compilers;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwen, when the Veritable Records of Taizu were compiled, Dong Lun and Wang Jing were chief compilers;

sentences.zh: 升與高遜誌為副總裁官；

translations.literal: Sheng and Gao Xunzhi were deputy chief compilers;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Gao Xunzhi were deputy compilers;

sentences.zh: 李貫、王紳、胡子昭、楊士奇、羅恢、程本立為纂修官。

translations.literal: Li Guan, Wang Shen, Hu Zizhao, Yang Shiqi, Luo Hui, and Cheng Benli were editing compilers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guan, Wang Shen, Hu Zizhao, Yang Shiqi, Luo Hui, and Cheng Benli served as editors.

sentences.zh: 皆一時選。

translations.literal: All were the finest men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: All were the finest scholars of the day.

sentences.zh: 燕師渡江，朝廷遣使請割地。

translations.literal: When the Yan army crossed the Yangzi, the court sent envoys to request a territorial settlement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army crossed the Yangzi, the court sent envoys to sue for a territorial settlement.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was refused.

sentences.zh: 升聞而慟哭，與家人訣，自縊死。

translations.literal: On hearing this Sheng wept bitterly, took leave of his family, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng heard this he wept bitterly, bade his family farewell, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 殉難諸臣，升死最先。

translations.literal: Among the ministers who died for the cause, Sheng was the first to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Among the martyred ministers, Sheng was the first to die.

sentences.zh: 其後陳瑛奏諸臣逆天命，效死建文君，請行追戮，亦首及升雲。

translations.literal: Later Chen Ying memorialized that many ministers had defied Heaven's mandate and died for the Jianwen emperor, requesting posthumous punishment; Sheng's name was also listed first.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chen Ying memorialized that many ministers had defied Heaven's mandate and died for Jianwen, asking for posthumous punishment; Sheng's name headed the list.

sentences.zh: 時為瑛追論者，有魏冕等。

translations.literal: At that time among those whom Ying sought to punish posthumously were Wei Mian and others.
translations.idiomatic: Among those Chen Ying sought to punish posthumously were Wei Mian and others.

sentences.zh: 冕官御史。

translations.literal: Mian held the office of censor.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was a censor.

sentences.zh: 燕兵犯闕，都督徐增壽徘徊殿廷，有異志。

translations.literal: When the Yan army assaulted the palace, the regional commander Xu Zengshou lingered in the hall with ulterior intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army stormed the palace, Regional Commander Xu Zengshou lingered in the hall, clearly harboring treacherous intent.

sentences.zh: 冕率同官毆之，與大理丞鄒瑾大呼，請速加誅。

translations.literal: Mian led his fellow officials in beating him, and together with the Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zou Jin cried out, begging that he be executed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Mian led his colleagues in beating him, and with Assistant Director of Justice Zou Jin shouted for his immediate execution.

sentences.zh: 明日，宮中火起。

translations.literal: The next day fire broke out in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: 有勸冕降者，厲聲叱之。

translations.literal: When someone urged Mian to surrender, he rebuked him in a harsh voice.
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged Mian to submit, he shouted him down.

sentences.zh: 遂自殺，瑾亦死。

translations.literal: He then killed himself, and Jin also died.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his own life, and Jin died as well.

sentences.zh: 瑾、冕皆永豐人。

translations.literal: Jin and Mian were both natives of Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Mian were both from Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 其同里鄒樸，官秦府長史。

translations.literal: Their fellow townsman Zou Pu held the post of Chief Secretary of the Prince of Qin's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Their fellow townsman Zou Pu was Chief Secretary to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 聞瑾死，憤甚，不食卒。

translations.literal: On hearing of Jin's death he was filled with rage, refused food, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of Jin's death he was so enraged that he stopped eating and died.

sentences.zh: 或曰即瑾子也。

translations.literal: Some say he was Jin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Some say he was Jin's son.

sentences.zh: 又都給事中龔泰，義烏人。

translations.literal: There was also the Chief Supervising Secretary Gong Tai, a native of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Chief Supervising Secretary Gong Tai, from Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 由鄉薦起家。

translations.literal: He began his career through provincial recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through provincial recommendation.

sentences.zh: 燕王入金川門，泰被縛，以非奸黨釋，不殺。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan entered through the Jinchuan Gate, Tai was bound, but because he was not counted among the traitor faction he was released and not killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan entered through the Jinchuan Gate, Tai was bound, but because he was not counted among the traitor faction he was released unharmed.

sentences.zh: 自投城下死。

translations.literal: He threw himself from the city wall and died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself from the wall and died.

sentences.zh: 泰嘗遊學宮，狂人擠之，溺池中幾死，弗校。

translations.literal: Tai once visited the school precinct; a madman jostled him and he nearly drowned in a pool, yet he did not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the school precinct a madman jostled him into a pool and he nearly drowned, yet he bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 人服其量。

translations.literal: People admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: People admired his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 是修外和內剛，誌操卓犖。

translations.literal: Shixiu was outwardly mild and inwardly firm, with lofty resolve and outstanding integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu was gentle in manner but steely within, with lofty resolve and outstanding integrity.

sentences.zh: 非其義，一介不茍得也。

translations.literal: What was not right he would not accept even in the smallest measure.
translations.idiomatic: He would not accept even the smallest gain that was not rightfully his.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「忠臣不計得失，故言無不直；

translations.literal: He once said: "A loyal minister does not reckon gain and loss, and therefore nothing he says is not straight;
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "A loyal minister does not weigh gain and loss, and so nothing he says is anything but straight;

sentences.zh: 烈女不慮死生，故行無不果。」

translations.literal: a woman of fierce integrity does not consider life and death, and therefore nothing she does is not carried through.
translations.idiomatic: a woman of fierce integrity does not weigh life and death, and so nothing she does fails to be carried through.

sentences.zh: 嘗輯古今忠節事為《觀感錄》。

translations.literal: He once compiled ancient and modern tales of loyalty and integrity into the Record of Stirred Feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled ancient and modern tales of loyalty and integrity into the Record of Stirred Feelings.

sentences.zh: 其學自經史百家，陰陽醫卜，靡不通究。

translations.literal: His learning ranged from the classics and histories through the hundred schools to yin-yang lore, medicine, and divination—there was none he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: His learning ranged from the classics and histories through the hundred schools to yin-yang lore, medicine, and divination—there was almost nothing he had not mastered.

sentences.zh: 為文援筆立就而雅贍條達。

translations.literal: In writing he took up the brush and finished at once, with elegance, richness, and lucid order.
translations.idiomatic: In writing he could take up the brush and finish at once, with elegance, fullness, and lucid order.

sentences.zh: 初與士奇、縉、靖及金幼孜、黃淮、胡儼約同死。

translations.literal: At first he had agreed with Shiqi, Jin, Jing, Jin Youzi, Huang Huai, and Hu Yan to die together.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had pledged with Shiqi, Jin, Jing, Jin Youzi, Huang Huai, and Hu Yan to die together.

sentences.zh: 臨難，惟是修竟行其誌雲。

translations.literal: When crisis came, only Shixiu in the end carried out his pledge.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis came, only Shixiu in the end kept his word.

sentences.zh: 程本立，字原道，崇德人。

translations.literal: Cheng Benli, styled Yuandao, was a native of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Benli, whose style was Yuandao, came from Chongde.

sentences.zh: 先儒頤之後。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of the former Confucian Cheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from the Neo-Confucian master Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 父德剛，負才氣不仕。

translations.literal: His father Degang possessed talent and spirit but would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Degang was gifted and proud, and refused office.

sentences.zh: 元將路成兵過皂林，暴掠。

translations.literal: When the Yuan general Lu Cheng's army passed Zaolin, they plundered violently.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan general Lu Cheng's troops passed through Zaolin, they plundered wildly.

sentences.zh: 德剛為陳利害。

translations.literal: Degang set forth the advantages and harms for him.
translations.idiomatic: Degang laid out the costs and benefits for him.

sentences.zh: 成悅，戢其部眾。

translations.literal: Cheng was pleased and restrained his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was pleased and reined in his men.

sentences.zh: 俗奏，官之，辭去。

translations.literal: The people memorialized and he was offered office, but he declined and left.
translations.idiomatic: The people petitioned for him to be given office, but he declined and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 本立少有大誌，讀書不事章句。

translations.literal: Benli from youth had great resolve; in reading he did not pursue mere textual glosses.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Benli had great ambition; in his studies he did not chase mere textual glosses.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，旌孝子，太祖嘗謂之曰：「學者爭務科舉，以窮經為名而無實學。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era he was commended as a filial son; the Founding Emperor once said to him: "Scholars all strive for the examinations, taking exhaustive study of the classics as a name yet lacking real learning.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu he was honored as a filial son; Taizu once told him, "Scholars all chase the examinations, claiming exhaustive mastery of the classics while lacking real learning.

sentences.zh: 子質近厚，當誌聖賢之學。」

translations.literal: Your nature is nearly substantial; you should set your heart on the learning of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: Your character is solid; you should devote yourself to the learning of the sages.

sentences.zh: 本立益自力。

translations.literal: Benli strove all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Benli redoubled his efforts.

sentences.zh: 聞金華朱克修得朱熹之傳於許謙，往從之遊。

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhu Kexiu of Jinhua had received Zhu Xi's transmission from Xu Qian, he went to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Zhu Kexiu of Jinhua had received Zhu Xi's teaching from Xu Qian, he went to study with him.

sentences.zh: 舉明經、秀才。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a Classicist and as a xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as a Classicist and as a cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 除秦府引禮舍人，賜楮幣、鞍馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Guiding Ceremonial Attendant of the Prince of Qin's establishment and was granted paper money and saddle horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Guiding Ceremonial Attendant in the Prince of Qin's household and was given paper money and horses.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官，服除，補周府禮官，從王之開封。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he left office; when mourning ended he was reassigned as a ritual officer of the Prince of Zhou's establishment and followed the prince to Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; when mourning ended he was reassigned as a ritual officer to the Prince of Zhou and followed him to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 二十年春進長史。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he was advanced to Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twentieth year he was promoted to Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 從王入覲。

translations.literal: He accompanied the prince to audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the prince to court.

sentences.zh: 坐累，謫雲南馬龍他郎甸長官司吏目。

translations.literal: Through implication in a case he was banished to the post of clerk in the Malong Talang Chief's Office in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Through implication in a case he was banished to a clerkship at the Malong Talang Chief's Office in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 留家大梁，攜一仆之任。

translations.literal: He left his family in Daliang and went to his post with a single servant.
translations.idiomatic: He left his family in Daliang and took only one servant to his post.

sentences.zh: 土酋施可伐煽百夷為亂，本立單騎入其巢，諭以禍福，諸酋鹹附。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Shi Kefa incited the hundred Yi peoples to revolt; Benli rode alone into their lair, admonished them with fortune and misfortune, and all the chiefs submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribal chief Shi Kefa stirred the Yi peoples to revolt, Benli rode alone into their stronghold, warned them of the consequences, and all the chiefs submitted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復變。

translations.literal: Before long they rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 西平侯沐英、布政使張紞知本立賢，屬行縣典兵事，且撫且禦。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying and the Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Hong, knowing Benli's worth, entrusted him to tour the counties and oversee military affairs, pacifying while defending.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying and Administration Commissioner Zhang Hong, recognizing Benli's ability, put him in charge of touring the counties and military affairs, pacifying while defending.

sentences.zh: 自楚雄、姚安抵大理、永昌鶴慶、麗江。

translations.literal: From Chuxiong and Yao'an he reached Dali, Yongchang, Heqing, and Lijiang.
translations.idiomatic: From Chuxiong and Yao'an he ranged through Dali, Yongchang, Heqing, and Lijiang.

sentences.zh: 山行野宿，往來綏輯凡九年，民夷安業。

translations.literal: Traveling mountains and sleeping in the wild, for nine years in all he went back and forth pacifying and organizing, and both Chinese and tribesmen lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling through mountains and sleeping in the open, for nine years he went back and forth pacifying the region until both settlers and tribesmen lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 三十一年奏計京師。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he reported to the capital for the annual review.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he went to the capital for the annual review.

sentences.zh: 學士董倫、府尹向寶交薦之。

translations.literal: The Academician Dong Lun and the Prefect Xiang Bao both recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Dong Lun and Prefect Xiang Bao both recommended him.

sentences.zh: 征入翰林，預修《太祖實錄》，遷右僉都御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned into the Hanlin Academy, took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor, and was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Hanlin, helped compile the Veritable Records of Taizu, and was made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 俸入外，不通饋遺。

translations.literal: Beyond his salary he accepted no gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond his salary he accepted no gifts.

sentences.zh: 建文三年坐失陪祀，貶官，仍留纂修。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwen, for failing to attend a sacrificial ceremony he was demoted but remained to continue compilation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen year three he was demoted for missing a sacrificial ceremony but kept on with the compilation work.

sentences.zh: 《實錄》成，出為江西副使。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records were completed, he was sent out as Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records were finished, he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 未行，燕兵入，自縊死。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, the Yan army entered; he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the Yan army entered the capital and he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 黃觀，字伯瀾，一字尚賓，貴池人。

translations.literal: Huang Guan, styled Bolan, also styled Shangbin, was a native of Guichi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Guan, styled Bolan and also Shangbin, came from Guichi.

sentences.zh: 父贅許，從許姓。

translations.literal: His father married into the Xu family and took the Xu surname.
translations.idiomatic: His father had married into the Xu family and bore the Xu surname.

sentences.zh: 受學於元待制黃冔。

translations.literal: He received instruction from the Yuan Academician Huang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under the Yuan Academician Huang Kan.

sentences.zh: 冔死節，觀益自勵。

translations.literal: When Kan died for principle, Guan strove all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: When Kan died for principle, Guan drove himself harder still.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，貢入太學。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era he was recommended and entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu he was recommended into the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 繪父母墓為圖，贍拜輒淚下。

translations.literal: He painted his parents' tombs as a picture; whenever he gazed upon it in veneration tears would fall.
translations.idiomatic: He painted his parents' graves into a picture, and whenever he looked at it in devotion he wept.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，會試、廷試皆第一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he ranked first in both the metropolitan and palace examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he placed first in both the metropolitan and palace examinations.

sentences.zh: 累官禮部右侍郎，乃奏復姓。

translations.literal: Rising through offices to Right Vice Minister of Rites, he then memorialized to restore his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Vice Minister of Rites and then memorialized to restore his original surname.

sentences.zh: 建文初，更官制，左、右侍中次尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen the official system was changed; the Left and Right Chamberlains ranked next after the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwen the official system was changed so that the Left and Right Chamberlains ranked just below the ministers.

sentences.zh: 改觀右侍中，與方孝孺等並親用。

translations.literal: Guan was made Right Chamberlain and, together with Fang Xiaoru and others, was employed in close confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was made Right Chamberlain and, with Fang Xiaoru and others, was used in the emperor's inner circle.

sentences.zh: 燕王舉兵，觀草制，諷其散軍歸藩，敕身謝罪，辭極詆斥。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan raised troops, Guan drafted the edict, admonishing him to disband his army and return to his fief, come in person to apologize, with language extremely abusive.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan rebelled, Guan drafted the edict urging him to disband his army, return to his fief, and come in person to apologize, in language of fierce denunciation.

sentences.zh: 四年奉詔募兵上遊，且督諸郡兵赴援。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, by imperial order he raised troops upstream and also supervised the forces of the various prefectures coming to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was ordered to raise troops upstream and to hurry the forces of the various prefectures to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 至安慶，燕王已渡江入京師，下令暴左班文職奸臣罪狀，觀名在第六。

translations.literal: When he reached Anqing, the Prince of Yan had already crossed the Yangzi and entered the capital; an order was issued publicizing the crimes of the civil traitors of the Left Shift, and Guan's name stood sixth.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Anqing, the Prince of Yan had already crossed the Yangzi and taken the capital; an order publicized the crimes of the civil traitors of the Left Shift, with Guan's name sixth on the list.

sentences.zh: 既而索國寶，不知所在，或言：「已付觀出收兵矣！」

translations.literal: Then the imperial seals were sought but could not be found; some said: "They have already been entrusted to Guan, who went out to gather troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Then the imperial seals were sought but could not be found; some said, "They were already entrusted to Guan when he went out to gather troops!"

sentences.zh: 命有司追捕，收其妻翁氏並二女給象奴。

translations.literal: Orders were given for the authorities to pursue and arrest him; his wife Lady Weng and two daughters were seized and given to elephant keepers.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities were ordered to pursue him; his wife Lady Weng and two daughters were seized and given to elephant keepers.

sentences.zh: 奴索釵釧市酒肴，翁氏悉與之持去，急攜二女及家屬十人，投淮清橋下死。

translations.literal: The keepers demanded hairpins and bracelets to buy wine and food; Lady Weng gave them all and went away with them, then hurriedly took her two daughters and ten members of the household and drowned themselves beneath the Huaiqing Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The keepers demanded jewelry to buy wine and food; Lady Weng gave them everything, then hurried away with her two daughters and ten family members and drowned themselves beneath the Huaiqing Bridge.

sentences.zh: 觀聞金川門不守，嘆曰：「吾妻有誌節，必死。」

translations.literal: When Guan heard that the Jinchuan Gate could not be held, he sighed: "My wife has resolve and integrity; she is sure to die."
translations.idiomatic: When Guan heard that the Jinchuan Gate had fallen, he sighed, "My wife has resolve and integrity; she is sure to die."

sentences.zh: 招魂，葬之江上。

translations.literal: He summoned her spirit and buried her by the river.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned her spirit and buried her by the river.

sentences.zh: 命舟至羅剎磯，朝服東向拜，投湍急處死。

translations.literal: He ordered a boat to the Luosha Reef, put on court dress and bowed facing east, then cast himself into the swift current and died.
translations.idiomatic: He had a boat take him to Luosha Reef, dressed in court robes and bowed facing east, then threw himself into the swift current and died.

sentences.zh: 觀弟覯，先匿其幼子，逃他處。

translations.literal: Guan's younger brother Jian first hid his infant son and fled elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's younger brother Jian first hid his infant son and fled elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 或云覯妻畢氏孀居母家，遺腹生子，故黃氏有後於貴池。

translations.literal: Some say Jian's wife Lady Bi lived as a widow in her mother's home, bore a posthumous son, and thus the Huang clan had descendants in Guichi.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Jian's wife Lady Bi lived as a widow in her mother's home, bore a posthumous son, and so the Huang line continued in Guichi.

sentences.zh: 初，觀妻投水時，嘔血石上，成小影，陰雨則見，相傳為大士像。

translations.literal: At first, when Guan's wife threw herself into the water, she vomited blood onto a stone, forming a small image that appeared in rainy weather; it was handed down as an image of the Bodhisattva.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan's wife drowned, she vomited blood onto a stone, leaving a small image that appeared in rainy weather; tradition held it to be an image of Guanyin.

sentences.zh: 僧舁至庵中。

translations.literal: Monks carried it into a hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: Monks carried it into a chapel.

sentences.zh: 翁氏見夢曰：「我黃狀元妻也。」

translations.literal: Lady Weng appeared in a dream and said: "I am the wife of the Huang zhuangyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Weng appeared in a dream and said, "I am the wife of the Huang zhuangyuan."

sentences.zh: 比明，沃以水，影愈明，有愁慘狀。

translations.literal: By dawn, when water was poured on it, the image grew clearer, with a sorrowful and wretched aspect.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn, when water was poured on it, the image grew clearer, with a sorrowful, anguished look.

sentences.zh: 後移至觀祠，名翁夫人血影石。

translations.literal: Later it was moved to Guan's shrine and named the Blood-Shadow Stone of Lady Weng.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was moved to Guan's shrine and called the Blood-Shadow Stone of Lady Weng.

sentences.zh: 今尚存。

translations.literal: It still exists today.
translations.idiomatic: It still survives today.

sentences.zh: 王叔英，字原采，黃巖人。

translations.literal: Wang Shuying, styled Yuancai, was a native of Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuying, whose style was Yuancai, came from Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，與楊大中、葉見泰、方孝孺、林右並征至。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era he was summoned to court together with Yang Dazhong, Ye Jiantai, Fang Xiaoru, and Lin You.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu he was summoned to court together with Yang Dazhong, Ye Jiantai, Fang Xiaoru, and Lin You.

sentences.zh: 叔英固辭歸。

translations.literal: Shuying firmly declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Shuying firmly declined and went home.

sentences.zh: 二十年以薦為仙居訓導，改德安教授。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, on recommendation he became Instructor of Xianju and was transferred to Professor of Dean.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was recommended as Instructor of Xianju and later made Professor of Dean.

sentences.zh: 遷漢陽知縣，多惠政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Hanyang, where he enacted many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Hanyang, where he enacted many benevolent policies.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，絕食以禱，立應。

translations.literal: In a year of drought he abstained from food to pray, and rain came at once.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year he fasted in prayer, and rain came at once.

sentences.zh: 建文時，召為翰林修撰。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen era he was summoned as Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen he was summoned as Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 上《資治八策》，曰：「務問學、謹好惡、辨邪正、納諫諍、審才否、慎刑罰、明利害、定法制」。

translations.literal: He submitted the Eight Policies for Ordering the Realm, saying: "Devote yourself to inquiry and learning, be careful in likes and dislikes, distinguish the crooked from the straight, accept remonstrance, judge talent and incapacity, be cautious in punishments, clarify benefit and harm, and fix laws and institutions."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the Eight Policies for Ordering the Realm: "Pursue learning, be careful in likes and dislikes, distinguish right from wrong, accept remonstrance, judge talent fairly, be cautious in punishments, clarify benefit and harm, and fix laws and institutions."

sentences.zh: 皆援證古今，可見之行事。

translations.literal: All were supported with proofs from antiquity and the present, visible in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Each point was backed with examples from past and present that could be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「太祖除奸剔穢，抑強鋤梗，如醫去病，如農去草。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Founding Emperor removed the treacherous and purged the foul, restrained the strong and uprooted the stubborn, like a physician removing disease, like a farmer clearing weeds.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Taizu removed the treacherous and purged corruption, restrained the strong and uprooted the stubborn, like a physician removing disease or a farmer clearing weeds.

sentences.zh: 去病急或傷體膚，去草嚴或傷禾稼。

translations.literal: If disease is removed too hastily the flesh may be harmed; if weeds are cleared too severely the grain may be injured.
translations.idiomatic: Remove disease too hastily and you may harm the body; clear weeds too harshly and you may injure the crop.

sentences.zh: 病去則宜調燮其血氣，草去則宜培養其根苗。」

translations.literal: When the disease is gone one should regulate and harmonize the blood and breath; when the weeds are gone one should nourish the roots and shoots.
translations.idiomatic: Once the disease is gone, regulate the body's vitality; once the weeds are gone, nourish the roots and shoots.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至淮，奉詔募兵。

translations.literal: When the Yan army reached the Huai, he received orders to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army reached the Huai, he was ordered to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 行至廣德，京城不守。

translations.literal: When he reached Guangde, the capital could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Guangde, the capital had fallen.

sentences.zh: 會齊泰來奔，叔英謂泰貳心，欲執之。

translations.literal: He met Qi Tai fleeing to join him; Shuying thought Tai had a divided heart and wished to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Tai fled to join him; Shuying suspected treachery and meant to seize him.

sentences.zh: 泰告以故，乃相持慟哭，共圖後舉。

translations.literal: Tai told him the reason; they then embraced and wept bitterly, planning together for a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: Tai explained what had happened; they embraced and wept, then planned what might still be done.

sentences.zh: 已，知事不可為，沐浴更衣冠，書絕命詞，藏衣裾間，自經於元妙觀銀杏樹下。

translations.literal: Before long, knowing the affair could not be accomplished, he bathed, changed his robes and cap, wrote his final words, hid them in the hem of his garment, and hanged himself beneath the ginkgo tree at the Yuanmiao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Soon seeing that nothing more could be done, he bathed, changed his robes and cap, wrote his final testament, hid it in his garment, and hanged himself beneath the ginkgo at Yuanmiao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 天臺道士盛希年葬之城西五里。

translations.literal: The Tiantai Daoist Sheng Xinian buried him five li west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiantai Daoist Sheng Xinian buried him five li west of the city.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：「人生穹壤間，忠孝貴克全。

translations.literal: His words read: "Born between heaven and earth, loyalty and filial piety are prized when fully fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: His testament read, "Born between heaven and earth, loyalty and filial piety are prized when fully achieved.

sentences.zh: 嗟予事君父，自省多過愆。

translations.literal: Alas, in serving lord and father, examining myself I find many faults.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, in serving lord and father, I find many faults in myself.

sentences.zh: 有誌未及竟，奇疾忽見纏。

translations.literal: I had resolve not yet fulfilled when a strange affliction suddenly seized me.
translations.idiomatic: I had resolve not yet fulfilled when a strange affliction suddenly seized me.

sentences.zh: 肥甘空在案，對之不下咽。

translations.literal: Rich fare lay empty on the table; facing it I could not swallow.
translations.idiomatic: Rich food lay untouched on the table; I could not swallow it.

sentences.zh: 意者造化神，有命歸九泉。

translations.literal: Perhaps the spirit of creation has decreed that my life return to the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps fate has decreed that my life return to the underworld.

sentences.zh: 嘗念夷與齊，餓死首陽巔。

translations.literal: I have thought of Boyi and Shuqi, who starved to death on the summit of Mount Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: I have thought of Boyi and Shuqi, who starved on Mount Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 周粟豈不佳，所見良獨偏。

translations.literal: Was the grain of Zhou not excellent? Yet their view alone was partial.
translations.idiomatic: Was Zhou grain not excellent? Yet their view alone was narrow.

sentences.zh: 高蹤渺難繼，偶爾無足傳。

translations.literal: Their lofty tracks are remote and hard to follow; chance acts are not worth transmitting.
translations.idiomatic: Their lofty example is remote and hard to follow; chance acts are not worth passing down.

sentences.zh: 千秋史官筆，慎勿稱希賢。」

translations.literal: For a thousand autumns the historian's brush—be careful never to call me a rare worthy.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand years the historian's brush—be careful never to call me a rare sage.

sentences.zh: 又題其案曰：「生既已矣，未有補於當時。

translations.literal: He also wrote on his desk: "In life it is already over; I have not aided the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote on his desk, "In life I have done no good for the age.

sentences.zh: 死亦徒然，庶無慚於後世。」

translations.literal: In death it is likewise vain; I hope only not to be ashamed before posterity.
translations.idiomatic: In death I can only hope not to be ashamed before posterity.

sentences.zh: 燕王稱帝，陳瑛簿錄其家。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan took the imperial title, Chen Ying inventoried his household.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan became emperor, Chen Ying inventoried his household.

sentences.zh: 妻金氏自經死，二女下錦衣獄，赴井死。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Jin hanged herself; his two daughters were sent to the Brocade-Clad Prison and threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Jin hanged herself; his two daughters were sent to the Brocade-Clad Prison and drowned themselves in a well.

sentences.zh: 叔英與孝孺友善，以道義相切劘。

translations.literal: Shuying was on friendly terms with Xiaoru and urged one another on in the way of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Shuying was close to Xiaoru, and they spurred one another on in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 建文初，孝孺欲行井田。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen, Xiaoru wished to implement the well-field system.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwen, Xiaoru wished to implement the well-field system.

sentences.zh: 叔英貽書曰：「凡人有才固難，能用其才尤難。

translations.literal: Shuying sent him a letter saying: "For any man to have talent is already difficult; to be able to use one's talent is still more difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Shuying wrote to him, "For any man to have talent is hard enough; to use that talent well is harder still.

sentences.zh: 子房於漢高，能用其才者也；

translations.literal: Zifang with Gaozu of Han was one who could use his talent;
translations.idiomatic: Zifang with Gaozu of Han was one who could use his talent;

sentences.zh: 賈誼於漢文，不能用其才者也。

translations.literal: Jia Yi with Emperor Wen of Han was one who could not use his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi with Emperor Wen of Han was one who could not use his.

sentences.zh: 子房察高帝可行而言，故高帝用之，一時受其利。

translations.literal: Zifang observed that Gaodi could act on his words and therefore spoke; Gaodi employed him, and for a time received his benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Zifang saw that Gaodi would act on good counsel and spoke accordingly; Gaodi used him and for a time profited from it.

sentences.zh: 雖親如樊、酈，信如平、勃，任如蕭、曹，莫得間焉。

translations.literal: Though as close as Fan and Li, as trusted as Ping and Bo, as relied upon as Xiao and Cao, none could come between them.
translations.idiomatic: Though men as close as Fan Kuai and Li Shang, as trusted as Chen Ping and Zhou Bo, as relied upon as Xiao He and Cao Shen, none could come between them.

sentences.zh: 賈生不察而易言，且言之太過，故絳、灌之屬得以短之。

translations.literal: Jia Yi did not observe and spoke lightly, and moreover spoke to excess, so men of the Zhou Bo and Guan Ying sort were able to find fault with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi spoke without reading the moment and spoke too boldly, so men like Zhou Bo and Guan Ying were able to attack him.

sentences.zh: 方今明良相值，千載一時。

translations.literal: Now ruler and minister of enlightenment meet—an occasion of a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Now a wise ruler and worthy minister meet—an occasion that comes once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 但事有行於古，亦可行於今者，夏時周冕之類是也。

translations.literal: But there are matters that were practicable in antiquity and are also practicable in the present—such as Xia seasons and Zhou caps.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some policies worked in antiquity and can work today as well—such as Xia calendar and Zhou ceremonial caps.

sentences.zh: 有行於古，不可行於今者，井田封建之類是也。

translations.literal: There are matters practicable in antiquity but not practicable in the present—such as well-fields and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Others worked in antiquity but cannot work today—such as the well-field system and feudal enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 可行者行，則人之從之也易，而民樂其利。

translations.literal: What can be done, if done, then men's following it is easy, and the people rejoice in its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When feasible measures are adopted, people follow readily and the common folk enjoy the gain.

sentences.zh: 難行而行，則從之也難，而民受其患。」

translations.literal: What is hard to do, if done, then following is hard, and the people suffer its harm."
translations.idiomatic: When impracticable measures are forced through, compliance is hard and the people suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 時井田雖不行，然孝孺卒用《周官》更易制度，無濟實事，為燕王藉口。

translations.literal: At the time the well-field system was not implemented, yet Xiaoru in the end used the Offices of Zhou to change and replace institutions, which did not aid practical affairs and gave the Prince of Yan a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: The well-field plan never took effect, yet Xiaoru still used the Offices of Zhou to overhaul institutions—doing nothing for practical governance while handing the Prince of Yan a pretext.

sentences.zh: 論者服叔英之識，而惜孝孺不能用其言也。

translations.literal: Commentators admired Shuying's discernment and regretted that Xiaoru could not use his words.
translations.idiomatic: Later commentators admired Shuying's judgment and lamented that Xiaoru would not heed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 時御史古田林英亦在廣德募兵，知事無濟，再拜自經。

translations.literal: At the time the investigating censor Lin Ying of Gutian was also in Guangde raising troops; knowing affairs would not succeed, he bowed twice and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the investigating censor Lin Ying of Gutian was also in Guangde raising troops; seeing there was no hope, he bowed twice and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 妻宋氏下獄，亦自經死。

translations.literal: His wife the Song clan was imprisoned and also hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Song was thrown into prison and hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至江上，善受詔統兵勤王，以書招鉞。

translations.literal: When the Yan army reached the Yangtze, Shan received an edict to command troops to relieve the throne and wrote a letter summoning Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces reached the Yangtze, Yao Shan received an edict to take command in the loyalist cause and wrote urging Yue to join him.

sentences.zh: 鉞知事不濟，辭以營葬畢乃赴。

translations.literal: Yue knew affairs would not succeed and declined on the grounds that he would come only after burial arrangements were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yue knew the cause was lost and pleaded that he could not come until he had finished the funeral arrangements.

sentences.zh: 既而童俊果以鎮江降燕。

translations.literal: Before long Tong Jun indeed surrendered Zhenjiang to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tong Jun did surrender Zhenjiang to the Yan forces.

sentences.zh: 鉞聞國變，杜門不出。

translations.literal: Yue heard of the change in the state and shut his door, not going out.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue heard that the dynasty had changed, he shut his doors and would not go out.

sentences.zh: 明年以戶科左給事中召，半途自投於水。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Left Assistant Director in the Household Section; halfway there he threw himself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned as Left Associate Censor of the Household Section; halfway to the capital he drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 以溺死聞，故其家得不坐。

translations.literal: It was reported that he drowned, so his family was spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because his death was reported as accidental drowning, his family escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 曾鳳韶，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Zeng Fengshao, a man of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Fengshao was a native of Luling.

sentences.zh: 洪武末年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the late Hongwu period.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the late Hongwu reign.

sentences.zh: 建文初，嘗為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he had served as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign he had served as an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 燕王稱帝，以原官召，不赴。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan took the imperial title, he was summoned to his former office but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan took the throne, he was recalled to his former post but refused to go.

sentences.zh: 又以侍郎召，知不可免，乃刺血書衣襟曰：「予生廬陵忠節之邦，素負剛鯁之腸。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Vice Minister; knowing he could not escape, he pricked blood and wrote on his collar, saying: "I was born in Luling, a land of loyalty and integrity, and have always borne an unyielding spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned again as a vice minister, he knew he could not escape; he pricked his finger and wrote in blood on his collar: "I was born in Luling, homeland of loyalty and integrity, and have always carried an unyielding heart.

sentences.zh: 讀書登進士第，仕宦至繡衣郎。

translations.literal: Through study I attained the jinshi degree and in official service rose to the embroidered-robe censor.
translations.idiomatic: Through study I won the jinshi degree and in office rose to the rank of embroidered-robe censor.

sentences.zh: 慨一死之得宜，可以含笑於地下，而不愧吾文天祥。」

translations.literal: I rejoice that a timely death is fitting and that I can go smiling to the underworld without shaming our Wen Tianxiang."
translations.idiomatic: I rejoice that death at the right moment is fitting—that I may go smiling to the shades without shaming our Wen Tianxiang.

sentences.zh: 囑妻李氏、子公望：「勿易我衣，即以此殮。」

translations.literal: He charged his wife Lady Li and son Gongwang: "Do not change my clothes; bury me in these alone."
translations.idiomatic: He told his wife Lady Li and his son Gongwang, "Do not change my clothes—bury me in them as they are."

sentences.zh: 遂自殺，年二十九。

translations.literal: He then killed himself, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his own life, aged twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 李亦守節死。

translations.literal: Li also died preserving her integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li also died upholding her integrity.

sentences.zh: 陳思賢，茂名人。

translations.literal: Chen Sixian, a man of Maoming.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sixian was a native of Maoming.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，為漳州教授，以忠孝大義勖諸生。

translations.literal: In the late Hongwu period he was professor at Zhangzhou and exhorted the students with the great principles of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Hongwu reign he served as professor at Zhangzhou, exhorting his students in loyalty, filial piety, and the great moral principles.

sentences.zh: 每部使者涖漳，參謁時必請曰：「聖躬安否？」

translations.literal: Whenever the touring inspector came to Zhangzhou, at the audience he would always request: "Is the Sagely Person well?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the touring inspector came to Zhangzhou, at the audience he would always ask: "Is His Majesty in good health?"

sentences.zh: 燕王登極詔至，慟哭曰：「明倫之義，正在今日。」

translations.literal: When the edict of the Prince of Yan's accession arrived, he wailed and said: "The meaning of human relations and righteousness hangs on this day."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict announcing the Prince of Yan's accession arrived, he wailed and said, "The bonds of human relations and righteousness are tested today."

sentences.zh: 堅臥不迎詔。

translations.literal: He lay abed firmly and did not welcome the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He lay abed and steadfastly refused to receive the edict.

sentences.zh: 率其徒吳性原、陳應宗、林玨、鄒君默、曾廷瑞、呂賢六人，即明倫堂為舊君位，哭臨如禮。

translations.literal: Leading his six disciples Wu Xingyuan, Chen Yingzong, Lin Jue, Zou Junmo, Zeng Tingrui, and Lü Xian, they at once set up the former emperor's seat in the Hall of Bright Principles and mourned according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He led six disciples—Wu Xingyuan, Chen Yingzong, Lin Jue, Zou Junmo, Zeng Tingrui, and Lü Xian—to set up a mourning seat for the former emperor in the Hall of Bright Principles and weep according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 有司執之送京師，思賢及六生皆死。

translations.literal: The authorities seized them and sent them to the capital; Sixian and the six students all died.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities arrested them and sent them to the capital; Sixian and all six students were executed.

sentences.zh: 六生皆龍溪人。

translations.literal: The six students were all men of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: All six students were natives of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，提學副使邵銳立祠祀思賢，以六生侑食。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period the Education Vice Commissioner Shao Rui erected a shrine to Sixian, with the six students as spirit companions.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing reign the education vice commissioner Shao Rui built a shrine to Sixian, with the six students as attendant spirits in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又臺州有樵夫，日負薪入市，口不貳價。

translations.literal: There was also in Taizhou a woodcutter who daily carried firewood to market and never charged two prices at the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizhou there was also a woodcutter who daily carried firewood to market and never haggled over the price.

sentences.zh: 聞燕王即帝位，慟哭投東湖死。

translations.literal: Hearing the Prince of Yan had taken the imperial throne, he wailed and threw himself into East Lake to die.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the Prince of Yan had taken the throne, he wailed and drowned himself in East Lake.

sentences.zh: 而溫州樂清亦有樵夫，聞京師陷，其鄉人卓侍郎敬死，號慟投於水。

translations.literal: In Yueqing of Wenzhou there was also a woodcutter who, hearing the capital had fallen and that Vice Minister Zhuo Jing of his district had died, wailed and threw himself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: In Yueqing, Wenzhou, there was another woodcutter who, hearing the capital had fallen and that Vice Minister Zhuo Jing of his home district had died, wailed and threw himself into the water.

sentences.zh: 二樵皆逸其名。

translations.literal: The names of both woodcutters are lost.
translations.idiomatic: The names of both woodcutters are unknown.

sentences.zh: 程通，績溪人。

translations.literal: Cheng Tong, a man of Jixi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tong was a native of Jixi.

sentences.zh: 嘗上書太祖，乞除其祖戍籍。

translations.literal: He once memorialized Taizu begging removal of his grandfather from military-guard registration.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized Taizu begging to remove his grandfather from frontier-guard registration.

sentences.zh: 詞甚哀，竟獲請。

translations.literal: His words were very plaintive, and in the end his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His plea was deeply moving, and in the end his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 已，授遼府紀善。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Recorder of the Liao Princedom.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed recorder of the Liao princedom.

sentences.zh: 燕師起，從王泛海歸京師，上封事數千言，陳禦備策，進左長史。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, he followed the prince across the sea to the capital and submitted a sealed memorial of several thousand characters setting forth defensive measures; he was promoted to Left Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces rose, he followed the prince by sea to the capital and submitted a sealed memorial of several thousand characters on defense; he was promoted to left chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，從王徙荊州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he followed the prince in transfer to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign he followed the prince in relocation to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 有言其前上封事多指斥者。

translations.literal: Someone said his earlier sealed memorial had largely denounced and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that his earlier sealed memorial had been full of denunciation.

sentences.zh: 械至，死於獄。

translations.literal: He was shackled and brought; he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was shackled and brought to the capital, where he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 家屬戍邊。

translations.literal: His family members were banished to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His family was banished to frontier guard duty.

sentences.zh: 並捕其友人徽州知府黃希範，論死，籍其家。

translations.literal: His friend too was seized—Huang Xifan, prefect of Huizhou—condemned to death and his household registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Huang Xifan, prefect of Huizhou, was also arrested, sentenced to death, and his household property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 葉惠仲，臨海人。

translations.literal: Ye Huizhong, a man of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Huizhong was a native of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 與兄夷仲並有文名，以知縣征修《太祖實錄》，遷知南昌府。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Yizhong were both famed for literature; summoned as magistrate to compile the Veritable Records of Taizu, he was transferred to prefect of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Yizhong were both renowned for letters; summoned as magistrate to help compile the Veritable Records of Taizu, he was later made prefect of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，坐直書《靖難》事，族誅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, for writing plainly about the Pacification of Difficulties, his entire clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle, for writing plainly about the Pacification of Difficulties, his entire clan was put to death.

sentences.zh: 黃彥清，歙人。

translations.literal: Huang Yanqing, a man of She.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yanqing was a native of She.

sentences.zh: 官國子博士，以名節自勵。

translations.literal: He served as Erudite of the National University and urged himself on by reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He served as erudite of the National University and held himself to the highest standards of reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 坐在梅殷軍中私謚建文帝，誅死。

translations.literal: For privately posthumously titling the Jianwen Emperor while in Mei Yin's army, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: For privately conferring a posthumous title on the Jianwen Emperor while serving in Mei Yin's army, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 蔡運，南康人。

translations.literal: Cai Yun, a man of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yun was a native of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 歷官四川參政。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Administrative Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administrative commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 勁直不諧於俗，罷歸。

translations.literal: Upright and stern, out of harmony with the vulgar, he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and uncompromising, ill at ease with worldly ways, he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 復起知賓州，有惠政。

translations.literal: He was again appointed and served as magistrate of Binzhou, where he had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed magistrate of Binzhou, where his rule was benevolent.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，亦追論奸黨死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he too was pursued and condemned as a traitor faction and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle he too was prosecuted as a traitor faction and put to death.

sentences.zh: 石允常，寧海人。

translations.literal: Shi Yunchang, a man of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yunchang was a native of Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 官河南僉事，廉介有聲。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Commissioner in Henan, renowned for integrity and sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice commissioner in Henan, famed for integrity and moral courage.

sentences.zh: 坐事謫常州同知。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted to vice prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 建文末，帥兵防江。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwen he led troops to defend the river.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jianwen reign he led troops to defend the Yangtze line.

sentences.zh: 軍潰，棄官去。

translations.literal: When the army collapsed he abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the army collapsed he abandoned his post and fled.

sentences.zh: 後追錄廢周藩事，系獄二年。

translations.literal: Later he was pursued and recorded for the matter of abolishing the Zhou princedom and imprisoned two years.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was prosecuted for his role in abolishing the Zhou princedom and imprisoned for two years.

sentences.zh: 免死戍邊。

translations.literal: Death was remitted and he was banished to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared execution and banished to frontier guard duty.

sentences.zh: 高巍，遼州人，尚氣節，能文章。

translations.literal: Gao Wei, a man of Liaozhou, prized integrity and could write.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wei was a native of Liaozhou who prized integrity and was skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 母蕭氏有痼疾，巍左右侍奉，至老無少懈。

translations.literal: His mother the Xiao clan had a chronic illness; Wei attended her at left and right until old age without the slightest slackening.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Xiao suffered a chronic illness; Wei attended her constantly until her old age without the slightest slackening.

sentences.zh: 母死，蔬食廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he ate vegetables and dwelt by the tomb in a hut for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he ate only vegetables and dwelt in a mourning hut by her tomb for three years.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，旌孝行，由太學生試前軍都督府左斷事。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period his filial conduct was commended; from Grand Academy student he was tested as Left Adjudicator of the Forward Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign his filial conduct was officially commended; as a Grand Academy student he was tested and appointed left adjudicator of the Forward Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 疏墾河南、山東、北平荒田。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reclaim wasteland in Henan, Shandong, and northern Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to reclaim wasteland in Henan, Shandong, and the northern Ping region.

sentences.zh: 又條上抑末技、慎選舉、惜名器數事。

translations.literal: He also submitted several items on curbing the last crafts, careful selection, and treasuring titles of honor.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted proposals on curbing minor crafts, careful selection of officials, and treasuring titles of honor.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉納之。

translations.literal: Taizu praised and adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised and adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 尋以決事不稱旨，當罪，減死戍貴州關索嶺。

translations.literal: Soon because his judgments did not accord with the intent, he was liable to punishment; death was reduced and he was banished to guard Guan Suoling in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his judgments failed to please the throne; though liable to death, the sentence was reduced to banishment to guard Guan Suoling in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 特許弟侄代役，曰：「旌孝子也。」

translations.literal: He was specially permitted younger brothers and nephews to serve in his stead, with the words: "This honors a filial son."
translations.idiomatic: He was specially allowed younger brothers and nephews to serve his term of exile, with the remark, "This honors a filial son."

sentences.zh: 及惠帝即位，上疏乞歸田裏。

translations.literal: When the Huaidi Emperor took the throne, he memorialized begging to return to his village fields.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huaidi Emperor took the throne, he memorialized begging to return to his fields in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遼州知州王欽應詔辟巍。

translations.literal: Before long the prefect of Liaozhou Wang Qin responded to the imperial summons and recruited Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Qin, prefect of Liaozhou, answered the imperial call and recruited Wei.

sentences.zh: 巍因赴吏部上書論時政。

translations.literal: Wei therefore went to the Ministry of Personnel and memorialized on current policies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei therefore went to the Ministry of Personnel and submitted a memorial on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 用事者方義削諸王，獨巍與御史韓郁先後請加恩。

translations.literal: Those in power were at the time righteously curtailing the princes; Wei alone with Investigating Censor Han Yu successively pleaded to add favor.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power were then bent on curtailing the princes; Wei alone, with the investigating censor Han Yu, successively pleaded to show them greater favor.

sentences.zh: 略曰：「高皇帝分封諸王，此之古制。

translations.literal: In summary: "The High Emperor enfeoffed the princes—this follows ancient systems.
translations.idiomatic: In summary he wrote: "The High Emperor enfeoffed the princes in accord with ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 既皆過當，諸王又率多驕逸不法，違犯朝制。

translations.literal: The enfeoffments were all excessive, and the princes moreover mostly were arrogant, dissolute, and lawless, violating court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The grants were all excessive, and the princes for the most part grew arrogant, dissolute, and lawless, violating court regulations.

sentences.zh: 不削，朝廷綱紀不立；

translations.literal: If not curtailed, the court's discipline and law cannot be established;
translations.idiomatic: If they are not curtailed, the court's discipline cannot be upheld;

sentences.zh: 削之，則傷親親之恩。

translations.literal: if curtailed, then the affection of kin wounds the affection of kin.
translations.idiomatic: yet if they are curtailed, the bonds of kinship are wounded.

sentences.zh: 賈誼曰：『欲天下治安，莫如眾建諸侯而少其力。』

translations.literal: Jia Yi said: 'If one wishes the realm to be secure, nothing is better than to multiply the enfeoffed princes while lessening their power.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi said, 'If you wish the realm to be secure, nothing is better than to multiply the feudal lords while diminishing their power.

sentences.zh: 今盍師其意，勿行晁錯削奪之謀，而效主父偃推恩之策。

translations.literal: Now why not take him as model and not carry out Chao Cuo's plan of curtailment and seizure but emulate Lord Father Yan's policy of extending favor.
translations.idiomatic: Why not follow his intent today—avoid Chao Cuo's policy of seizure and curtailment, and instead emulate Lord Father Yan's strategy of extending favor.

sentences.zh: 在北諸王，子弟分封於南；

translations.literal: For princes in the north, sons and younger brothers are enfeoffed in the south;
translations.idiomatic: For princes in the north, let sons and younger brothers be enfeoffed in the south;

sentences.zh: 在南，子弟分封於北。

translations.literal: for those in the south, sons and younger brothers are enfeoffed in the north.
translations.idiomatic: for those in the south, let sons and younger brothers be enfeoffed in the north.

sentences.zh: 如此則藩王之權，不削而自削矣。

translations.literal: In this way the princes' power, without being cut, is cut of itself.
translations.idiomatic: In this way princely power would diminish of itself without direct curtailment.

sentences.zh: 臣又願益隆親親之禮，歲時伏臘使人饋問。

translations.literal: Your subject also wishes further to augment the rites of affection among kin—at the year's end, on the winter solstice and grave-sweeping days, send men with gifts to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also urges that the rites honoring kin be further elevated—at the winter solstice and grave-sweeping seasons send envoys with gifts to inquire after them.

sentences.zh: 賢者下詔褒賞之。

translations.literal: For the worthy, issue an edict to praise and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: For the worthy, issue edicts of praise and reward.

sentences.zh: 驕逸不法者，初犯容之，再犯赦之，三犯不改，則告太廟廢處之。

translations.literal: For the arrogant, dissolute, and lawless—in the first offense tolerate them, in the second pardon them; if in the third they do not reform, then report to the Imperial Ancestors' Temple and depose them.
translations.idiomatic: For the arrogant and lawless, tolerate the first offense, pardon the second; if after a third they still do not reform, report to the Imperial Ancestors' Temple and depose them.

sentences.zh: 豈有不順服者哉！」

translations.literal: Would there be any who would not submit!"
translations.idiomatic: Would any then fail to submit!"

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝頷之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the Emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was presented, the Emperor nodded in approval.

sentences.zh: 已而燕兵起，命從李景隆出師參贊軍務。

translations.literal: Before long the Yan army rose; he was ordered to follow Li Jinglong on campaign as aide in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Yan forces rose; he was ordered to follow Li Jinglong on campaign as an aide in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 巍復上書，言：「臣願使燕。

translations.literal: Wei again memorialized, saying: "Your subject wishes to be sent to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei memorialized again, saying, "Your subject begs to be sent as envoy to Yan.

sentences.zh: 披忠膽，陳義禮，曉以禍福，感以親親之誼，令休兵歸藩。」

translations.literal: Lay open loyal guts, set forth righteous ritual, enlighten with calamity and blessing, move with the affection of kin, and order a ceasefire and return to the princedom."
translations.idiomatic: I would lay bare my loyal heart, set forth righteousness and ritual, explain the blessings and calamities at stake, appeal to the bonds of kinship, and persuade him to cease arms and return to his princedom."

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was stirred by his words and assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was stirred by his words and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 巍至燕，自稱：

translations.literal: Wei reached Yan and styled himself:
translations.idiomatic: When Wei reached Yan, he introduced himself:

sentences.zh: 國朝處士高巍再拜上書燕王殿下：太祖上賓，天子嗣位，布維新之政，天下愛戴，皆曰「內有聖明，外有藩翰，成、康之治，再見於今矣。」

translations.literal: Scholar of Our Dynasty Gao Wei again bows and memorializes to the Prince of Yan: Taizu ascended to the upper guest; the Son of Heaven succeeded the throne and proclaimed renewing policies; the realm adores him, all saying "Within there is sagely enlightenment, without there are princely screens—the governance of Cheng and Kang is seen again today."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wei, a scholar of the dynasty, again bows and memorializes to Your Highness the Prince of Yan: Taizu has ascended on high; the Son of Heaven has succeeded the throne and proclaimed renewing policies. The realm adores him, all saying, "Within there is a sage ruler, without there are princely bulwarks—the governance of the Cheng and Kang era is seen again in our day."

sentences.zh: 不謂大王顯與朝廷絕，張三軍，抗六師，臣不知大王何意也。

translations.literal: I did not expect Your Highness plainly to break with the court, marshal three armies, and resist the six hosts—I do not know what Your Highness intends.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that Your Highness would openly break with the court, marshal three armies, and resist the imperial hosts. I do not know what Your Highness intends.

sentences.zh: 今在朝諸臣，文者智輳，武者勇奮，執言仗義，以順討逆。

translations.literal: Now the various ministers at court: civil ones gather wisdom, martial ones surge in courage, uphold speech and rely on righteousness, use obedience to punish rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Today the ministers at court cluster wisdom among the civil officials and summon courage among the military; they speak out for righteousness and take the side of legitimacy to punish rebellion.

sentences.zh: 勝敗之機明於指掌。

translations.literal: The mechanism of victory and defeat is clear as on the palm.
translations.idiomatic: The odds of victory and defeat are as plain as what lies in the palm of one's hand.

sentences.zh: 皆云大王「藉口誅左班文臣，實則吳王濞故智，其心路人所共知。」

translations.literal: All say of Your Highness, "Using as pretext the execution of left-rank civil ministers, but in fact the old stratagem of King of Wu Liu Bi—his heart is what passersby on the road all know alike."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone says of Your Highness, "You claim to be punishing the civil ministers of the left rank, but in truth you are replaying the old trick of King of Wu Liu Bi—and your intent is plain to any passerby on the road."

sentences.zh: 巍竊恐奸雄無賴，乘隙奮擊，萬一有失，大王得罪先帝矣。

translations.literal: Wei secretly fears that villainous heroes and ruffians will seize the gap and strike fiercely; if there is any slip, Your Highness will offend the Former Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I fear in secret that unscrupulous adventurers will seize the opening and strike hard; should anything go wrong, Your Highness will have wronged the Former Emperor.

sentences.zh: 今大王據北平，取密雲，下永平，襲雄縣，掩真定。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness holds Beiping, took Miyun, descended Yongping, raided Xiongxian, covered Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: You now hold Beiping, have taken Miyun, descended on Yongping, raided Xiongxian, and pressed toward Zhending.

sentences.zh: 雖易若建瓴，然自兵興以來，業經數月，尚不能出蕞爾一隅地。

translations.literal: Though easy as tipping a pitcher from the high eaves, yet since troops were raised it has already been several months, still unable to exit this tiny corner of land.
translations.idiomatic: Though each move may seem as easy as tipping a jar from a high roof, since the war began several months have passed and you still cannot break out of this paltry corner of territory.

sentences.zh: 且大王所統將士，計不過三十萬。

translations.literal: Moreover the generals and soldiers Your Highness commands—counting no more than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the officers and men under Your Highness's command number no more than three hundred thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 以一國有限之眾應天下之師，亦易罷矣。

translations.literal: Using one state's limited multitude to meet the realm's armies—it is also easy to be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: To pit the limited forces of a single principality against the armies of the whole realm is to invite exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 大王與天子義則君臣，親則骨肉，尚生離間。

translations.literal: Your Highness and the Son of Heaven—in righteousness are ruler and subject, in affection are flesh and bone—yet still produce estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Between Your Highness and the Son of Heaven, duty makes you ruler and subject and blood makes you kin—yet you have still bred estrangement.

sentences.zh: 況三十萬異姓之士能保其同心協力，效死於殿下乎？

translations.literal: How much more can three hundred thousand non-kin soldiers guarantee they will cooperate with one heart and pledge death to Your Highness?
translations.idiomatic: How much less can three hundred thousand men of other surnames be counted on to stand as one and die for Your Highness?

sentences.zh: 巍每念至此，未始不為大王灑泣流涕也。

translations.literal: Whenever Wei thinks of this he never has not wept tears for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of this, I cannot help but weep for Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 願大王信巍言：上表謝罪，再修親好。

translations.literal: May Your Highness trust Wei's words: memorialize to confess guilt and again repair kinship.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to heed my words: submit a memorial of repentance and restore the bonds of kinship.

sentences.zh: 朝廷鑒大王無他，必蒙寬宥。

translations.literal: The court discerning Your Highness has no other intent will surely receive clemency.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court sees that Your Highness harbors no other design, you will surely be granted mercy.

sentences.zh: 太祖在天之靈亦安矣。

translations.literal: Taizu's spirit in Heaven will also be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's spirit in Heaven will also be at rest.

sentences.zh: 倘執迷不悟，舍千乘之尊，捐一國之富，恃小勝，忘大義，以寡抗眾，為僥幸不可成之悖事，巍不知大王所稅駕也。

translations.literal: If stubbornly unawakened, abandon the honor of a thousand chariots, discard a state's wealth, rely on small victories, forget great righteousness, use the few against the many, do the perverse thing of fortunate impossibility—Wei does not know where Your Highness's tax chariot will alight.
translations.idiomatic: If you cling to error, cast aside the dignity of a great prince, squander a realm's wealth, trust in petty victories and forget the greater right, pit the few against the many, and pursue a reckless gamble that cannot succeed—I do not know where Your Highness's road will end.

sentences.zh: 況大喪未終，毒興師旅，其與泰伯、夷、齊求仁讓國之義不大逕庭乎？

translations.literal: Moreover great mourning not yet ended, poisonously raising armies—how is this not greatly at odds with Taibo, Bo Yi, and Shu Qi seeking benevolence and yielding the state?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, while the great mourning is not yet complete you have venomously raised armies—how far is that from the spirit in which Taibo, Bo Yi, and Shu Qi sought humanity and yielded the realm?

sentences.zh: 雖大王有肅清朝廷之心，天下不無篡奪嫡統之議。

translations.literal: Though Your Highness has a mind to purge the court, the realm cannot be without talk of usurping the legitimate succession.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Highness means only to purge the court, the realm will not lack talk of usurping the legitimate succession.

sentences.zh: 即幸而不敗，謂大王何如人？
