translations.literal: Even if by fortune undefeated—what kind of person would they call Your Highness?
translations.idiomatic: Even if by good fortune you were not defeated, what sort of man would the world call Your Highness?

sentences.zh: 巍白髮書生，蜉蝣微命，性不畏死。

translations.literal: Wei is a white-haired book scholar, ephemeral life, by nature not fearing death.
translations.idiomatic: I am a white-haired scholar with a mayfly's span of life, and by nature I do not fear death.

sentences.zh: 洪武十七年蒙太祖高皇帝旌臣孝行。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Hongwu received the Hongwu Taizu High Emperor's commending the subject's filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Hongwu era, Taizu the High Emperor commended my filial conduct.

sentences.zh: 巍竊自負：既為孝子，當為忠臣。

translations.literal: Wei secretly took pride: having been a filial son, ought to be a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: I privately took pride in this: having been a filial son, I ought to be a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 死忠死孝，巍至願也。

translations.literal: Die loyal, die filial—Wei's utmost wish.
translations.idiomatic: To die loyal and die filial—that is my deepest wish.

sentences.zh: 如蒙賜死，獲見太祖在天之靈，巍亦可以無愧矣。

translations.literal: If granted death, obtaining to see Taizu's spirit in Heaven—Wei also can be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: If I am granted death and may behold Taizu's spirit in Heaven, I too can die without shame.

sentences.zh: 書數上，皆不報。

translations.literal: Letters sent several times—all without reply.
translations.idiomatic: He sent several letters, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 已而景隆兵敗，巍自拔南歸。

translations.literal: Then Jinglong's army defeated, Wei himself freed and returned south.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinglong's army was defeated, Wei broke free and made his way south.

sentences.zh: 至臨邑，遇參政鐵鉉，相持痛哭。

translations.literal: Reaching Linyi, met administering prefect Tie Xuan, held each other weeping.
translations.idiomatic: At Linyi he met the administering prefect Tie Xuan, and the two embraced and wept.

sentences.zh: 奔濟南，誓死拒守，屢敗燕兵。

translations.literal: Ran to Jinan, vowed death in defense, repeatedly defeated Yan armies.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to Jinan, swore to defend it unto death, and repeatedly defeated the Yan forces.

sentences.zh: 及京城破，巍自經死驛舍。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Wei hanged himself dead in the courier station.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, he hanged himself in a courier station.

sentences.zh: 郁疏略曰：

translations.literal: Yu summary memorial said:
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianning's summary memorial read:

sentences.zh: 諸王親則太祖遺體，貴則孝康皇帝手足，尊則陛下叔父。

translations.literal: The various princes—in kinship are Taizu's legacy body, in nobility are Emperor Xiaokang's brothers, in honor are Your Majesty's uncles.
translations.idiomatic: The princes are, in kinship, the bodily legacy of Taizu; in rank, the brothers of Emperor Xiaokang; in honor, Your Majesty's uncles.

sentences.zh: 使二帝在天之靈，子孫為天子，而弟與子遭殘戮，其心安乎？

translations.literal: Suppose the two emperors' spirits in Heaven saw descendants as Son of Heaven yet younger brothers and sons suffer slaughter—would their hearts be at peace?
translations.idiomatic: If the spirits of the two emperors in Heaven saw their descendant enthroned as Son of Heaven while younger brothers and sons were slaughtered, could their hearts be at peace?

sentences.zh: 臣每念至此，未嘗不流涕也。

translations.literal: Your subject whenever thinks of this never has not shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever your subject thinks of this, he cannot help but weep.

sentences.zh: 此皆豎儒偏見，病藩封太重，疑慮太深，乃至此。

translations.literal: All this is pedantic scholars' biased views, sick over enfeoffment too heavy, suspicions too deep, reaching to this.
translations.idiomatic: All of this stems from the narrow prejudices of petty scholars who fault the enfeoffments as too weighty and suspicions as too deep, until matters have come to this pass.

sentences.zh: 夫唇亡齒寒，人人自危。

translations.literal: When lips perish teeth grow cold—every person in self-danger.
translations.idiomatic: When the lips are gone the teeth grow cold—every man feels himself in peril.

sentences.zh: 周王既廢，湘王自焚，代府被摧，而齊臣又告王反矣。

translations.literal: Zhou King already deposed, Xiang King self-immolated, Dai mansion destroyed, and Qi state's minister again reported the prince rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhou was already deposed, the Prince of Xiang burned himself, the house of Dai was broken, and then a minister of Qi again reported that a prince had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 為計者必曰：「兵不舉則禍必加」。

translations.literal: Those making plans must say: "If troops are not raised then calamity must be added."
translations.idiomatic: Those who weighed their options were bound to say, "If we do not take up arms, disaster is sure to follow."

sentences.zh: 是朝廷執政激之使然。

translations.literal: It is the court administering government that stirred them to thus.
translations.idiomatic: It was the conduct of those who held power at court that drove them to this.

sentences.zh: 燕舉兵兩月矣，前後調兵不下五十余萬，而一矢無獲。

translations.literal: Yan raised troops two months already; before and after mobilizing troops no less than five hundred thousand-plus, yet not one arrow obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yan has been at war for two months; more than five hundred thousand troops have been mobilized in all, yet not a single arrow has been won.

sentences.zh: 謂之國有謀臣可乎？

translations.literal: Call this the state having plotting ministers—acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: Can this be called a realm that possesses wise counselors?

sentences.zh: 經營既久，軍興輒乏，將不效謀，士不效力。

translations.literal: Management already long, raising armies always lacking, generals not effective in counsel, soldiers not exerting effort.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign has dragged on; whenever armies are raised supplies run short; generals do not put counsel into effect, and soldiers do not give their strength.

sentences.zh: 徒使中原無辜赤子困於轉輸，民不聊生，日甚一日。

translations.literal: Only made Central Plains innocent red infants trapped in transport levies, people not able to live, day more severe by day.
translations.idiomatic: It only leaves the innocent common people of the Central Plains exhausted by transport levies; the people cannot make a living, and each day grows worse than the last.

sentences.zh: 九重之憂方深，而出入帷幄與國事者，方且揚揚自得。

translations.literal: The ninefold's worry just deep, yet those entering and exiting the curtain with state affairs are just complacent and self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Anxiety within the palace grows daily, yet those who move in and out of the inner councils and manage state affairs remain smug and pleased with themselves.

sentences.zh: 彼其勸陛下削藩國者，果何心哉？

translations.literal: Those their advising Your Majesty to reduce princedom states—what intent indeed?
translations.idiomatic: Those who urged Your Majesty to weaken the princedoms—what were they truly after?

sentences.zh: 諺曰：「親者割之不斷，疏者續之不堅。」

translations.literal: The proverb says: "Kin—cut it and it will not sever; distant—join it and it will not solid."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says, "Kin you may cut but cannot sever; the distant you may join but cannot make firm."

sentences.zh: 殊有理也。

translations.literal: Extremely has reason.
translations.idiomatic: There is deep truth in that.

sentences.zh: 陛下不察，不待十年，悔無及矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty not inspecting—not wait ten years, regret without time.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not discern this, within ten years you will regret it when it is too late.

sentences.zh: 臣至愚，感恩至厚，不敢不言。

translations.literal: Your subject utmost foolish, gratitude utmost thick, dare not not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is utterly foolish, but the grace shown him is profound, and he dares not remain silent.

sentences.zh: 幸少垂洞鑒，興滅繼絕，釋代王之囚，封湘王之墓，還周王於京師，迎楚、蜀為周公。

translations.literal: Fortunate little let penetrate mirror, revive extinct continue severed, release Dai King's prisoner, seal Xiang King's tomb, return Zhou King to the capital, welcome Chu and Shu as Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to lend a little of your penetrating insight: restore the fallen and continue the cut off; release the Prince of Dai from prison, restore the tomb of the Prince of Xiang, return the Prince of Zhou to the capital, and welcome the Princes of Chu and Shu as Duke of Zhou did.

sentences.zh: 俾各命世子持書勸燕，罷兵守藩，以慰宗廟之靈。

translations.literal: So each order heir sons to hold letters urging Yan, cease troops guard princedoms, to comfort the ancestral temple's spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Let each prince command his heir to carry letters urging Yan to lay down arms and guard his fief, so as to comfort the spirits of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 明詔天下，撥亂反正，篤厚親親，宗社幸甚。

translations.literal: Bright decree the realm, pacify chaos return to righteousness, sincere thick kinship, ancestral altar greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Issue a clear edict to the realm, set right the turmoil, and show sincere regard for kin—the altars of state would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: Not listened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 燕師渡江，郁棄官遁去，不知所終。

translations.literal: Yan army crossed the Jiang, Yu abandoned office fled away, unknown where ended.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army crossed the Yangzi, Gao Xianning abandoned his post and fled; no one knows his end.

sentences.zh: 王琎，字器之，日照人。

translations.literal: Wang Jin, styled Qizhi, a man of Rizhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, styled Qizhi, was a native of Rizhao.

sentences.zh: 博通經史，尤長於《春秋》。

translations.literal: Broadly penetrated classics and histories, especially excelled in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly versed in the classics and histories and was especially accomplished in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 初為教授，坐事謫遠方。

translations.literal: At first was an instructor, sat on affair banished to distant place.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as an instructor, but because of an offense was banished to a distant post.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，以賢能薦，授寧波知府。

translations.literal: At Hongwu's end, by worth and ability recommended, appointed Ningbo prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Hongwu era he was recommended for worth and ability and appointed prefect of Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 夜四鼓即秉燭讀書，聲徹署外。

translations.literal: At night at the fourth watch he took candle to read books, sound penetrating outside the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch each night he would take up a candle to read, and the sound of his voice carried beyond the yamen walls.

sentences.zh: 間詣學課諸生，諸生率四鼓起，誦習無敢懈。

translations.literal: Occasionally went to the school to lecture students; students all at fourth watch rose, reciting study none dared slack.
translations.idiomatic: He would sometimes go to the school to instruct the students, who all rose at the fourth watch to recite their lessons and dared not slacken.

sentences.zh: 毀境內淫祠，三皇祠亦在毀中，或以為疑。

translations.literal: Destroyed within the borders illicit shrines; Three Emperors shrine also was in the destruction, some took it doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: He demolished illicit shrines within his jurisdiction; the shrine to the Three Sovereigns was among those torn down, and some questioned this.

sentences.zh: 琎曰：「不當祠而祠曰『淫』，不得祠而祠曰『瀆』。

translations.literal: Jin said: "What ought not be enshrined yet is enshrined is called 'licentious'; what may not be enshrined yet is enshrined is called 'profane.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "To worship what ought not to be worshiped is licentious; to worship what one is not permitted to worship is profane.

sentences.zh: 惟天子得祭三皇，於士庶人無預，毀之何疑。」

translations.literal: Only the Son of Heaven may sacrifice to the Three Emperors; for gentlemen and commoners there is no part—destroy it what doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Only the Son of Heaven may sacrifice to the Three Sovereigns; scholars and commoners have no part in it—why hesitate to tear it down?"

sentences.zh: 自奉儉約，一日饌用魚羹，琎謂其妻曰：「若不憶吾啖草根時耶？」

translations.literal: He himself upheld frugality; one day the meal used fish broth, Jin told his wife: "Do you not recall when I ate grass roots?"
translations.idiomatic: He lived frugally himself. One day fish broth was served at table, and Jin said to his wife, "Have you forgotten the days when I ate grass roots?"

sentences.zh: 命撤而埋之，人號「埋羹太守。」

translations.literal: Ordered it withdrawn and buried; people called him "Buried Broth Grand Governor."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it cleared away and buried, and people nicknamed him the Grand Governor Who Buried the Broth."

sentences.zh: 燕師臨江，琎造舟艦謀勤王，為衛卒縛至京。

translations.literal: When Yan army reached the Jiang, Jin built boats and warships plotting to aid the king, was by guard soldiers bound and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army reached the Yangzi, Jin built warships to aid the loyalist cause and was bound by garrison troops and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 成祖問：「造舟何為？」

translations.literal: Chengzu asked: "Building boats for what?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu asked, "Why were you building boats?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「欲泛海趨瓜洲，阻師南渡耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Wished to cross the sea and hurry to Guazhou, block the army's south crossing—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I meant to put to sea and make for Guazhou, to block your army's crossing south—that is all."

sentences.zh: 帝亦不罪，放還裏，以壽終。

translations.literal: The Emperor also did not punish, released to return home, ended by longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish him, released him to his home, and he died at a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 周縉，字伯紳，武昌人。

translations.literal: Zhou Jin, styled Boshen, a man of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jin, styled Boshen, was a native of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 以貢入太學，授永清典史，攝令事。

translations.literal: By tribute entered the Imperial Academy, appointed Yongqing clerk of records, acted magistrate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy as a tribute student and was appointed clerk of records at Yongqing, where he handled the magistrate's duties.

sentences.zh: 成祖舉兵，守令相率迎降。

translations.literal: Chengzu raised troops; prefects and magistrates followed one another in welcoming surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu raised his army, prefects and magistrates one after another went out to welcome him and surrender.

sentences.zh: 永清地尤近，縉獨為守禦計。

translations.literal: Yongqing's territory especially near, Jin alone made plans to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing lay especially close to the front, and Jin alone made plans for defense.

sentences.zh: 已，度不可為，懷印南奔。

translations.literal: Then, estimating it could not be done, clasped the seal and ran south.
translations.idiomatic: Soon seeing that resistance was impossible, he took the official seal and fled south.

sentences.zh: 道聞母卒，歸終喪。

translations.literal: On the road heard mother died, returned to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he heard that his mother had died and returned home to complete the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 燕兵已迫，糾義旅勤王，聞京師不守，乃走匿。

translations.literal: Yan troops already pressing, gathered righteous troops to aid the king; heard the capital not held, then ran and hid.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army was already pressing close; he rallied loyal volunteers to aid the throne, but when he heard that the capital had fallen he fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 吏部言：「前北平所屬州縣官朱寧等二百九十人，當皇上『靖難』，俱棄職逃亡。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel said: "Former Beiping subordinate prefecture and county officials Zhu Ning and others two hundred ninety persons, when His Majesty 'pacified difficulties,' all abandoned office and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel reported, "Formerly, two hundred ninety officials of prefectures and counties under Beiping, including Zhu Ning, all abandoned their posts and fled when His Majesty carried out the Pacification Campaign.

sentences.zh: 宜置諸法。」

translations.literal: Ought to be placed within the law."
translations.idiomatic: They should be punished according to law."

sentences.zh: 詔令入粟贖罪，遣戍興州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered grain tribute to redeem guilt, sent to garrison Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed them to redeem their guilt with grain payments and sent them to garrison duty at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 有司遂捕縉，械送戍所。

translations.literal: The responsible offices then arrested Jin, shackled and sent to the garrison place.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities then arrested Jin, put him in fetters, and sent him to the garrison.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，子代還，年八十而沒。

translations.literal: Dwelling several years, son replaced and returned; at age eighty then died.
translations.idiomatic: After several years his son took his place on the garrison roster and he returned home; he died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 朱寧等皆無考。

translations.literal: Zhu Ning and others all without further record.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing further is recorded of Zhu Ning and the others.

sentences.zh: 牛景先，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Niu Jingxian—unknown what place man.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jingxian was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 官御史。

translations.literal: Office: censor.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of censor.

sentences.zh: 金川門開，易服宵遁，卒於杭州僧寺。

translations.literal: Jinchuan Gate opened, changed clothes and fled by night, died at a Hangzhou monk temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinchuan Gate was opened he changed his clothes and fled by night, and died in a Buddhist temple at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 已而窮治齊、黃黨，籍其家。

translations.literal: Then thoroughly prosecuted the Qi and Huang factions, registered their households.
translations.idiomatic: Later the authorities pursued the Qi and Huang factions to the end and confiscated their households.

sentences.zh: 燕兵之入，一夕朝臣縋城去者四十余人。

translations.literal: When Yan troops entered, in one night court ministers who rope-descended the wall and left were more than forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army entered the capital, more than forty court officials let themselves down from the city wall in a single night and fled.

sentences.zh: 其姓名爵裏莫可得而考。

translations.literal: Their names, surnames, ranks, and native places cannot be obtained and examined.
translations.idiomatic: Their names, titles, and native places cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 然世相傳，有程濟及河西傭、補鍋匠之屬。

translations.literal: Yet the age mutually transmits there were Cheng Ji and the west-of-river hired hand, pot-mender, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Yet tradition has handed down the names of Cheng Ji, the hired hand from west of the river, the pot-mender, and others of that sort.

sentences.zh: 河西傭，不知何許人。

translations.literal: West-of-river hired hand—unknown what place man.
translations.idiomatic: The hired hand from west of the river was a man of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 建文四年冬，披葛衣行乞金城市中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwen winter, wore ramie clothes and begged walking in the Jin capital city.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year of the Jianwen era he wore a hemp cloak and went begging through the streets of the capital.

sentences.zh: 已，至河西為傭於莊浪魯氏。

translations.literal: Then, reaching west of the river, became a hired hand for the Lu clan of Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went west of the river and hired himself out to the Lu family of Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 取直買羊裘，而以故葛衣覆其上，破縷縷不肯棄。

translations.literal: Took wages and bought a sheep-fur coat, yet with the old ramie clothes covered atop it; tattered threads he would not abandon.
translations.idiomatic: He used his wages to buy a sheepskin coat but laid his old hemp cloak over it, and would not cast aside its ragged threads.

sentences.zh: 力作倦，輒自吟哦，或夜聞其哭聲。

translations.literal: When hard labor tired him he would himself chant and hum, or at night one heard his weeping sound.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew weary from hard labor he would chant to himself, and at night people sometimes heard him weeping.

sentences.zh: 久之，有京朝官至，識傭，欲與語，走南山避之。

translations.literal: After long time, a capital court official arrived, recognized the hired hand, wished to speak with him—ran to South Mountain to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while a capital official came, recognized the hired hand, and wished to speak with him; he fled to the southern hills to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 或問京朝官：「傭何人？」

translations.literal: Someone asked the capital court official: "The hired hand—what person?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked the capital official, "Who is this hired hand?"

sentences.zh: 官亦不答。

translations.literal: The official also did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The official would not answer.

sentences.zh: 在莊浪數年，病且死，呼主人屬曰：「我死勿殮。

translations.literal: Dwelling at Zhuanglang several years, ill and about to die, called the master and entrusted: "When I die do not encoffin.
translations.idiomatic: After several years at Zhuanglang he fell ill and, near death, called his employer and said, "When I die, do not prepare my body for burial.

sentences.zh: 西北風起，火我，勿埋我骨。」

translations.literal: When northwest wind rises, burn me, do not bury my bones."
translations.idiomatic: When the northwest wind rises, burn me—do not bury my bones."

sentences.zh: 魯家從其言。

translations.literal: The Lu family followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu family did as he said.

sentences.zh: 補鍋匠者，常往來夔州、重慶間。

translations.literal: The pot-mender—often came and went between Kuizhou and Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: The pot-mender often traveled back and forth between Kuizhou and Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 業補鍋，凡數年，川中人多識之。

translations.literal: Practiced pot-mending; in all several years, people in the river region mostly knew him.
translations.idiomatic: He plied the trade of pot-mending for several years, and many in Sichuan came to know him.

sentences.zh: 一日，於夔州市遇一人，相顧愕然。

translations.literal: One day in the market of Kuizhou he met a man; they stared at each other in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: One day in the Kuizhou market he met a man, and they stared at each other in shock.

sentences.zh: 已，相持哭，共入山巖中，坐語竟日。

translations.literal: Then they embraced and wept, went together into a mountain cave, and sat talking the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Then they embraced and wept, went into a mountain cave together, and talked all day.

sentences.zh: 復相持哭，別去。

translations.literal: Again they embraced and wept, then parted.
translations.idiomatic: They embraced and wept again, then parted.

sentences.zh: 其人即馮翁也。

translations.literal: That man was Old Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The man was Old Feng.

sentences.zh: 翁在夔以章句授童子，給衣食，能為古詩。

translations.literal: Feng in Kuizhou taught children through textual exegesis, provided food and clothing, and could compose ancient-style verse.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuizhou Feng taught boys through classical exegesis, provided for their food and clothing, and wrote old-style poetry.

sentences.zh: 詩後題「馬二子」，或「馬公」，或「塞馬先生」。

translations.literal: At the end of his poems he signed "Ma Erzi," or "Lord Ma," or "Master Sai Ma."
translations.idiomatic: He signed his poems "Ma Erzi," "Lord Ma," or "Master Sai Ma."

sentences.zh: 後二人皆不知所終。

translations.literal: Later neither man's end was known.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the fate of neither man was known.

sentences.zh: 又會稽有二隱者：一雲門僧，一若耶溪樵。

translations.literal: In Kuaiji there were also two recluses: a monk of Yunmen, and a woodcutter of the Ruoye Stream.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji there were also two recluses: a Yunmen monk and a woodcutter on the Ruoye Stream.

sentences.zh: 僧每泛舟賦詩，歸即焚之。

translations.literal: The monk would row a boat and compose poetry, then burn it on returning.
translations.idiomatic: The monk would row out and compose poetry, then burn it when he came home.

sentences.zh: 樵每於溪沙上以荻畫字，已，輒亂其沙。

translations.literal: The woodcutter would write characters on the stream sand with a reed, then always scramble the sand.
translations.idiomatic: The woodcutter would write on the stream sand with a reed, then always smear the sand away.

sentences.zh: 人有疑之者，從後抱持觀之，則皆孤臣去國之詞也。

translations.literal: When someone suspicious embraced him from behind to look, all were words of a lone minister leaving his state.
translations.idiomatic: When someone suspicious grabbed him from behind to read, every line was the lament of a loyal minister in exile.

sentences.zh: 時又有玉山樵者，居金華之東山，麻衣戴笠，終身不易。

translations.literal: At the time there was also the Yushan woodcutter, who lived on the eastern hill of Jinhua in hemp clothes and bamboo hat, never changing them all his life.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Yushan woodcutter, who lived on Jinhua's eastern hill in hemp clothes and a bamboo hat and never changed them all his life.

sentences.zh: 嘗為王姓者題詩曰「宗人」，故疑其王姓雲。

translations.literal: Once he inscribed a poem for a man surnamed Wang as "clansman," so people suspected he too was surnamed Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Once he inscribed a poem for a Wang as "kinsman," so people suspected he was a Wang as well.

sentences.zh: 雪庵和尚，人疑其為葉希賢，見《練子寧傳》。

translations.literal: The monk Xue'an—people suspected he was Ye Xixian; see the biography of Lian Zining.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Xue'an was thought by some to be Ye Xixian; see the biography of Lian Zining.

sentences.zh: 其後數十年，松陽王詔遊治平寺，於轉輪藏上得書一卷，載建文亡臣二十余人事跡。

translations.literal: Several decades later Wang Zhao of Songyang visited Zhiping Temple and obtained a scroll on the revolving sutra cabinet recording the deeds of more than twenty Jianwen loyalists in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Decades later Wang Zhao of Songyang visited Zhiping Temple and found a scroll on the revolving sutra cabinet recording more than twenty Jianwen loyalists in exile.

sentences.zh: 楮墨斷爛，可識者僅九人。

translations.literal: The paper and ink were broken and rotted; only nine could be identified.
translations.idiomatic: The paper and ink were decayed; only nine names could be made out.

sentences.zh: 梁田玉、梁良玉、梁良用、梁中節皆定海人，同族，同仕於朝。

translations.literal: Liang Tianyu, Liang Liangyu, Liang Liangyong, and Liang Zhongjie were all natives of Dinghai, of the same clan, and all served at court.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tianyu, Liang Liangyu, Liang Liangyong, and Liang Zhongjie were all from Dinghai, of one clan, and all served at court.

sentences.zh: 田玉，官郎中，京師破，去為僧。

translations.literal: Tianyu held the office of Director; when the capital fell he left and became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyu was a Director; when the capital fell he became a monk.

sentences.zh: 良玉，官中書舍人，變姓名，走海南，鬻書以老。

translations.literal: Liangyu was a Secretariat Drafter; he changed his name, fled to Hainan, and lived out his years selling books.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu was a Secretariat Drafter; he changed his name, fled to Hainan, and lived out his years selling books.

sentences.zh: 良用為舟師，死於水。

translations.literal: Liangyong was a boat master and died in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyong was a boat master and drowned.

sentences.zh: 中節好《老子》、《太玄經》，為道士。

translations.literal: Zhongjie loved the Laozi and the Classic of Supreme Mystery and became a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjie loved the Laozi and the Classic of Supreme Mystery and became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 何申、宋和、郭節，俱不知何許人，同官中書。

translations.literal: He Shen, Song He, and Guo Jie—all of unknown origin—were fellow Secretariat Drafters.
translations.idiomatic: He Shen, Song He, and Guo Jie—all of unknown origin—were fellow Secretariat Drafters.

sentences.zh: 申使蜀，至峽口聞變，嘔血，疽發背死。

translations.literal: Shen was sent to Shu; at the gorge mouth he heard of the upheaval, vomited blood, and died of a carbuncle on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was sent to Shu; at the gorge he heard of the upheaval, vomited blood, and died of a back carbuncle.

sentences.zh: 和及節挾卜筮書走異域，客死。

translations.literal: He and Jie took books of divination and fled to foreign lands, dying abroad.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jie fled abroad with divination texts and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 何洲，海州人。

translations.literal: He Zhou was a native of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhou came from Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 不知何官，亦去為卜者，客死。

translations.literal: His office is unknown; he too left to become a diviner and died abroad.
translations.idiomatic: His office is unknown; he too became a diviner and died abroad.

sentences.zh: 郭良，官籍俱無考，與梁中節相約棄官為道士。

translations.literal: Guo Liang's office and register cannot be ascertained; with Liang Zhongjie he agreed to abandon office and become Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Liang's office and origins cannot be verified; he and Liang Zhongjie agreed to abandon office and become Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 余十一人並失其姓名。

translations.literal: The remaining eleven all lost their names.
translations.idiomatic: The names of the other eleven were lost.

sentences.zh: 縉雲鄭僖紀其事，為《忠賢奇秘錄》，傳於世。

translations.literal: Zheng Xi of Jinyun recorded the affair in the Secret Record of Loyal Worthies, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi of Jinyun recorded the affair in the Secret Record of Loyal Worthies, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 及萬歷時，江南又有《致身錄》，雲得之茅山道書中。

translations.literal: By the Wanli era in Jiangnan there was also the Record of Devoted Lives, said to have been obtained from Daoist books on Mount Mao.
translations.idiomatic: By the Wanli era Jiangnan also had the Record of Devoted Lives, said to come from Daoist texts on Mount Mao.

sentences.zh: 建文時，侍書吳江史仲彬所述，紀帝出亡後事甚具。

translations.literal: It was related by Shi Zhongbin of Wujiang, attendant secretary in the Jianwen era, and records the emperor's flight in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: It was said to be by Shi Zhongbin of Wujiang, a Jianwen-era attendant secretary, and records the emperor's flight in great detail.

sentences.zh: 仲彬、程濟、葉希賢、牛景先皆從亡之臣。

translations.literal: Zhongbin, Cheng Ji, Ye Xixian, and Niu Jingxian were all ministers who followed the emperor in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongbin, Cheng Ji, Ye Xixian, and Niu Jingxian were all ministers who followed the emperor into exile.

sentences.zh: 又有廖平、金焦諸姓名，而雪庵和尚、補鍋匠等，具有姓名、官爵。

translations.literal: There were also names such as Liao Ping and Jin Jiao, while the monk Xue'an, the pot-mender, and others had both names and offices.
translations.idiomatic: It also named Liao Ping and Jin Jiao, while the monk Xue'an, the pot-mender, and others were given names and ranks.

sentences.zh: 一時士大夫皆信之。

translations.literal: For a time the scholar-officials all believed it.
translations.idiomatic: For a time scholar-officials all believed it.

sentences.zh: 給事中歐陽調律上其書於朝，欲為請謚立祠。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Ouyang Diaolu presented the book at court, wishing to request posthumous titles and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Ouyang Diaolu presented the book at court and sought posthumous titles and temples for them.

sentences.zh: 然考仲彬實未嘗為侍書，《錄》蓋晚出，附會不足信。

translations.literal: Yet investigation shows Zhongbin never actually served as attendant secretary; the Record was probably a late work, and its forced connections are not to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhongbin never actually served as attendant secretary; the Record was probably a late forgery and not to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：靖難之役，朝臣多捐軀殉國。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: In the Pacification campaign many court ministers gave their lives for the state.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: In the Pacification campaign many court ministers gave their lives for the state.

sentences.zh: 若王艮以下諸人之從容就節，非大義素明者不能也。

translations.literal: That men from Wang Gen downward could meet their end with such composure—only those to whom the great principle was clear from the first could do so.
translations.idiomatic: That men from Wang Gen onward could face death with such composure—only those steeped in the great principle could do so.

sentences.zh: 高巍一介布衣，慷慨上書，請歸藩服。

translations.literal: Gao Wei was but a commoner in plain cloth, yet boldly submitted a memorial asking the prince to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wei was only a commoner, yet boldly memorialized asking the prince to return to his fief.

sentences.zh: 其持論甚偉，又能超然遠引，晦跡自全，可稱奇士。

translations.literal: His argument was very grand, and he could also withdraw far away, hide his tracks, and preserve himself—a man who may be called extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His argument was bold, and he could also withdraw, hide his tracks, and preserve himself—a truly extraordinary man.

sentences.zh: 若夫行遯諸賢，雖其姓字雜出於諸家傳紀，未足征信，而忠義奇節，人多樂道之者。

translations.literal: As for the worthies in flight, though their surnames and names appear scattered in various family records and are not fully reliable, their loyal and righteous deeds are gladly told by many.
translations.idiomatic: As for the fugitive worthies, though their names appear scattered in various records and cannot be fully verified, people still love to tell of their loyal and heroic deeds.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「與其過而去之，寧過而存之。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "Better to err by preserving than to err by discarding.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "Better to err by preserving than to err by discarding.

sentences.zh: 亦足以扶植綱常，使懦夫有立誌也。

translations.literal: It is also enough to uphold the moral order and give faint-hearted men a resolve to stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: It is enough to uphold moral order and give timid men the will to stand firm.
